LESSON: STATISTICAL METHODS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GEOGRAPHY
Strand: Practical Geography
Topic 1.3: Statistical Methods
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Statistical Methods, part of Practical Geography in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 GEOGRAPHY.

Key inquiry question: How do we use statistics in day- to-day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Brainstorm the importance of statistics in Geography and share in class. - Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC or be allowed extra time to express their views on the importance of statistics. Those with postural difficulties could require appropriate positioning.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Brainstorm the importance of statistics in Geography and share in class. - Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC or be allowed extra time to express their views on the importance of statistics. Those with postural difficulties could require appropriate positioning.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Statistical Methods together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: The skill of research as the learner conducts library research on the

limitations of statistics in explaining geographical facts and writes notes

● Learning to Learn: The skill of investigation as the learner carries out research within the school on a selected

geographical topic

● Creativity and Imagination: The skill of asking questions as the learner role plays the methods of data

collection

● Digital Literacy: The skill of interacting with technology is enhanced as learners use digital resources to make

presentations of their research findings in class.

Values:
● Integrity: Learner exhibits honesty as they carry out research within the school on a selected geographical

topic

● Respect: Learner expresses patience as they brainstorm on the importance of statistics in Geography and

makes presentation in class

● Unity: Learner role play, in groups, the methods of data collection.

● Responsibility: Learners use digital resources to make presentations in class on the research findings.

● Social Cohesion: Learner works with others as they brainstorm on the importance of statistics in Geography
